independent_verification.claim_fidelity: Equation (32) uses the fixed radial cutoff, and Lemma 4.17 explicitly allows any C2,gamma height with values in [-1/2,1/2], then forms the inverse map and inverse Jacobian. The constant-height example directly satisfies that lemma's written assumptions.
independent_verification.independent_argument: For h=-1/3,t=9/10, phi(1/5)=0 and phi(1/2)=1 force zeta_t(e/5)=e/5=zeta_t(e/2). Both inputs are distinct interior points and t,h lie strictly inside the stated ranges. Independently, rho=sqrt(17/18)+(1/3)cos(2theta) has area pi because its mean square is 17/18+1/18=1; central symmetry centers it. Its height range lies inside (-1/2,1/2), and at theta=pi/2 the radius .5+.9*(sqrt(17/18)-4/3) lies in (0,1/4), producing the second collision. This latter example is not claimed to meet an arbitrary prescribed C3,gamma bound.
independent_verification.repair_verification: For M=||phi'||infty, M||h||infty<=1/2 gives dR_t/dr>=1/2. Since R_t= r near zero, R_t>0 for r>0; each ray maps strictly monotonically, angles are preserved, and det D zeta_t=(R_t/r)^(n-1)dR_t/dr>0. This proves a regular inverse and the stated boundary image.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Constant h gives genuine balls of radius 1-t/3 and analytic eigenvalues lambda_i(B)/(1-t/3)^2, so failure of this parametrization does not refute spectral analyticity. Pages 29,31,46â€“48 impose fixed C3,gamma control and sufficiently small L1 norm. Interpolation makes the sup norm small enough for the repair by reducing a dimensional constant, without introducing a new k exponent.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_grade: The chosen pullback feeds the local second-variation arguments, but their actual operative smallness supplies the missing condition. Minor appropriately records the overbroad auxiliary assertion; no principal stability theorem is disproved.
